events.title: Some under-25s should get fewer benefits, Milburn review to say
events.summary: Alan Milburn will publish his review next week Some young people could see reductions to the benefits they are entitled to under a radical overhaul of the welfare system to be recommended by a government-commissioned review. As reported in the Times, , external Alan Milburn's year-long report, to be published on Tuesday, is expected to recommend moving under-25s off the main sickness and disability benefits. Milburn, a former Labour health secretary, has been tasked by the government with helping reduce the one in eight 16 to 24 year-olds in the UK who are not in education, employment or training - otherwise known as "Neet". He said on Wednesday night that his plans would not be "pain-free" and would affect both existing and new claimants. His report is expected to say that under-25s should no longer be able to claim the health element of UK-wide universal credit - or personal independence payment (Pip), the main disability benefit in England and Wales. Disabled people in Scotland can claim the devolved Adult Disability Payment. Instead, under Milburn's plan, under-25s would receive an allowance on the same basic rate as universal credit. Some could be eligible for a new "additional cost allowance" to cover day-to-day costs related to their conditions. Some claimants would receive less under the plans - although the exact amounts will not be clear until early next year, when the government publishes legislation to implement the changes. People can claim Pip to help them with the additional cost of being disabled or living with long-term physical or mental health conditions. It is available to those both in and out of work. In his interim report, , external Milburn said survey data found that 19% of young people claiming disability or health benefits were in work. Milburn, a Labour MP from 1992 to 2010, is also expected to recommend an investment of billions into more employment support for young people, including work placements, job subsidies and one-to-one personal advisers. Those with more severe disabilities and unable to work would get a new benefit paid at a higher rate. Milburn told the Times: "Candidly, it could mean that some people will get less financial support at the beginning of their benefit claim than under the current system. "But actually, for young people, there's a different debate that we've got to resolve, which is whether the priority is their longer-term life chances or just their immediate shorter-term finances. "I think what the current system does [is] it prioritises the latter over the former. I believe that's the wrong choice and it needs to be the other way around." Speaking later on Thursday, Prime Minister Andy Burnham said young people would be given support "when they need it as teenagers rather than leaving them on benefits in their 20s". He added: "The principle that we will be working on is that we will guarantee support for young people and that is the whole basis on which we will proceed." Just under one million young people in the UK are Neets , data from the Office for National Statistics (ONS) from April to June suggests. This was a rise of 3% on the same period last year. Milburn's recommendations are likely to be backed by Prime Minister Andy Burnham but could prove controversial among Labour MPs, who opposed welfare changes last year under his predecessor Sir Keir Starmer. Dame Meg Hillier, who helped spearhead a backbench rebellion against Starmer's reforms, suggested she and her colleagues were broadly supportive this time around. "What happened last year was a cut was being proposed and none of us could explain to people what would happen to them," the Labour MP told the BBC. "Milburn has done some very good work on this so I'm giving him a fair wind," she added. But Bell Ribeiro-Addy, one of the Labour backbenchers who revolted last year, said she was "not sure" she could vote to cut the benefit entitlement of existing claimants. Tom Ashforth, a 19-year-old student at Sheffield Hallam University, receives both components of Pip at the higher rate. He said the financial support helps him manage additional expenses linked to his visual impairment, including prescriptions, mobility aids and accessible learning resources. "If I were to lose it, I would struggle to afford essential things," he said. Student Tom said he relies on the money he gets from Pip to support him through his time at university He said he believes decisions over disability benefits should be made on a case-by-case basis, rather than according to age. "You cannot assume that everyone under the age of 25 is in the same position," he said. In his Times interview, Milburn acknowledged that changing the rules for existing claimants would be "difficult politically" but stressed it was necessary. James Taylor, from disability equality charity Scope, said Pip was a "lifeline" and restricting access to it "won't make young disabled people's extra costs disappear".

events.title: Alice Huang tied to Nvidia’s biggest Chinese competitor
events.summary: Alice Huang, with whom ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang reportedly had a romantic relationship, has owned stakes in companies that have benefited Huawei, Nvidia's No. 1 competitor in China. The entanglement has not been previously reported and was first uncovered by private intelligence firm Tesari and shared exclusively with CNBC. The Huawei connection may add to questions about the consequences of the relationship, which has already been under scrutiny by policymakers due to U.S. intelligence reportedly alleging Alice Huang is a Chinese spy. Alleged Chinese spy Alice Huang may have owned stakes in businesses in China that benefited Nvidia's biggest competitor in China, Huawei, at the same time that she was in business with Nvidia and also reportedly having a romantic affair with its ousted CEO Jensen Huang . The connection between Alice Huang and Huawei was first discovered by analysts at private intelligence firm Tesari. The firm exclusively shared its findings with CNBC. Tesari, which uses artificial intelligence to collect evidence and specializes in national security investigations around the world, provides intelligence research to private companies and the U.S. government. This previously unreported entanglement may raise questions about Alice Huang's intent and conduct in her relationship with the CEO and whether Jensen Huang knew his romantic partner was closely connected with his competition. Jensen Huang has acknowledged having an affair, though the precise timing of his relationship with Alice Huang is unknown. The mysterious saga of Alice Huang involves a tangle of interlocking corporations and transactions that show her connection to entities that ultimately provided computing power to Huawei in China. Huawei is known as a Chinese government "state champion" in the technology and telecommunications sectors, meaning it receives enormous financial support from the government in Beijing so it can lower prices and undercut global competitors. It is considered a key part of the Chinese government's push for global technical dominance and is closely linked to the Chinese Communist Party. Businesses connected to Alice Huang were linked with supplying Nvidia computing power to Huawei, according to documents reviewed by CNBC, around the same time she and Jensen Huang were first publicly seen together, in December 2023. In 2024, Nvidia said Huawei was a top competitor , specifically in artificial intelligence chips including graphics processing units, central processing units and networking chips. Nvidia live updates: Jensen Huang agrees to testify before Congress following resignation Who is Colette Kress? Nvidia's finance chief steps in as interim CEO after Huang exit PRO: Buy Nvidia with 'both hands' because the valuation is at 'stupid' levels, says analyst Meeks Read what interim CEO Kress and board chair Harvey Jones wrote to Nvidia employees Jensen Huang's exit from Nvidia raises critical questions about the future of AI Analysis: Nvidia's leadership crisis tests the chipmaker's role as the 'central bank of AI' "This activity, which surfaced through our analysis of Alice's network, warrants a national security and [technology] counterproliferation investigation," said Brian Andersen, Tesari's vice president for national security applications and a former supervisory special agent with Homeland Security Investigations. If the Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry Security and Homeland Security Investigations found evidence that anyone transferred "controlled equipment" to Huawei without authorization, potential charges might include export-control violations, conspiracy and smuggling, Andersen said. The connection between Alice Huang and Huawei is so convoluted that analysts at Tesari told CNBC that based on their previous investigative experience, they suspect it was designed to deliberately obscure the relationship. Nvidia and Huawei did not respond to CNBC's requests for comment. Jensen Huang did not respond to a voicemail left on a mobile phone. Alice Huang could not be reached. According to Chinese corporate records and media reports compiled by Tesari and provided to CNBC, Alice Huang, whose Chinese name is Huang Le and who according to documents at the time was based in Hong Kong, in 2019 sold a cloud business she owned called Osmanthus to a Chinese gaming company called 7Road. A subsidiary of 7Road, which was based in Singapore, was spun off as "Megaspeed" in 2023 . Megaspeed would go on to become a key Nvidia customer, helping facilitate at least $7.5 billion in Nvidia chip shipments to Chinese firms, The Information reported Tuesday. As early as 2016, Alice Huang had also become a co-owner of a financial firm known as Shanghai Hexi , which heavily invests in tech and data centers. In 2021, Hexi in turn acquired 27 percent of a company called Shanghai Century Longteng, a data center developer, which Hexi held until 2024 .

events.title: Democrats launch Nvidia investigation, write scathing letter on Huang’s ‘scheme’ with Trump
events.summary: Democrats on Thursday opened an inquiry into how the Trump administration handled Nvidia’s chip sales to China. Earlier on Thursday, the company ousted its CEO Jensen Huang . He also agreed to testify to a different set of Republican-led Congressional committees. Huang was removed from the company he founded after he confessed to an extramarital affair with a woman accused of being a Chinese spy. (He has since been accused of having more affairs , with Nvidia employees.) The alleged Chinese spy, Alice Huang, was an executive of Nvidia customer Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company that U.S. officials suspect of helping route advanced Nvidia chips into China. The Democratic inquiry comes from Rep. Richard Neal (D-Mass.), the top Democrat on the House Ways and Means Committee, and Sen. Ron Wyden (D-Ore.), the top Democrat on the Senate Finance Committee. As the minority party, they can ask questions but can’t compel answers. Their humdinger of a letter to Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick asks the department to preserve records about an arrangement they find questionable and, they allege, illegal. “The scheme worked like this,” as the letter describes it. President Trump agreed to sales of Nvidia’s H200 chips to China as long as the chips, manufactured by Taiwan, were first shipped to the United States. On arriving, Trump added a tariff “effectively taking a cut of Nvidia’s sales to China through what appears to be an unconstitutional export tax system,” the letter said. Then the Commerce Department, under Lutnick, issued an export license. By the way, the deal between Trump and Nvidia to share revenue was public. In August 2025, Nvidia and AMD both agreed to share 15% of their revenue from chip sales to China with the U.S. government as part of a deal to secure export licenses, the AP reported at the time. But the letter questions why Lutnick continued to allow Megaspeed to buy chips even after he was reportedly informed by U.S. intelligence of their suspicions of Alice Huang and of Jensen Huang’s relationship with her. It questions why the department reportedly green-lit other Asian companies to buy Nvidia chips “with no physical presence at their listed addresses.” So the inquiry is aimed at the administration, not just at Nvidia and Huang. The letter also questions how Nvidia’s donations to Trump’s projects factored in. It notes that the export deal was approved after Trump learned of “Mr. Huang’s compromised position” in sleeping with an alleged spy, and after Nvidia donated $26 million toward Trump’s projects, including the ballroom. It appears to be asking if Trump used his knowledge of the affair to secure donations from Nvidia. Interestingly, in a “60 Minutes” interview with President Trump that aired on Sunday, Trump mentioned how he and his team had threatened an unnamed AI exec with jail , and after that, the exec “totally changed.” This Congressional investigation into Nvidia’s China sales and its dealings with Trump is the second one, so far, since news of the alleged spy affair broke. The Republican-led group involves leaders from the House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party, the House Committee on Foreign Affairs, and the House Intelligence Committee. That group has demanded that Huang come to them and testify in a closed-door session. They had threatened to subpoena him if he didn’t voluntarily agree. events.title: Donald Trump Jr exits as paid adviser for prediction market Kalshi
events.summary: Kalshi announces ‘mutual decision’ as Democrats say they plan to investigate Trump family’s investments Donald Trump Jr is no longer a paid adviser for Kalshi, the prediction market company said Thursday. Kalshi described it as a mutual business decision between the two parties that followed a decision by Trump Jr’s investment firm, 1789 Capital, to increase its investment in Kalshi’s biggest competitor Polymarket. But the announcement comes a week after Democrats were able to take control of both the House and Senate in the midterm elections. Democrats have said they planned to investigate the Trump family’s investments, including their business relationships with both prediction markets. “We have mutually agreed to end Don’s advisory role after his firm’s significant investment in a competitor this past summer,” said Dani Lever, a spokesperson for Kalshi. “We are grateful for his contributions in helping us market Kalshi to more customers.” The president’s eldest son became a paid “strategic adviser” for Kalshi shortly after President Trump was sworn into office for his second term in January 2025 and has been an investor in Polymarket since August 2025. Both companies have seen their popularity and use jump significantly in the past two years. At the same time, both companies have received favorable treatment from the White House. The Commodity Futures Trading Commission has backed the industry’s efforts to expand their products nationwide, including allowing their customers to trade sports-related contracts. Both companies have adamantly denied that the financial relationship between Polymarket, Kalshi and the Trumps played any role in how the industry has been regulated under this administration. 1789 Capital increased its investment in Polymarket this past August, as part of Polymarket’s latest fundraising round. It was this investment that started the conversation about ending Trump Jr’s advisory role with Kalshi.

events.title: Silicon Valley Is Still Defending Jensen Huang
events.summary: News of Jensen Huang’s affair with an alleged asset of China’s Ministry of State Security was first met with a muted response in Silicon Valley —including inside Nvidia itself. Huang’s resignation , after news of two other alleged romantic relationships with Nvidia staffers, has left both the company and the broader AI industry stunned . As revelations about Huang’s initial affair came out earlier this week, rank-and-file Nvidia employees at first pursued business as usual, according to two current and three former employees at the chipmaker, speaking anonymously to protect relationships at the company. They trusted the board to investigate and act accordingly, but few workers thought Huang would actually leave. Nvidia’s roughly 60,000 employees are loyal to the point that its global turnover rate is reportedly among the lowest in tech. Workers say they have heard it called having “green in your blood” or being “green-pilled” or on “team green,” referring to the company’s signature color. Huang was the company’s soul and the founder who stuck with it through challenges for 33 years. Employees appreciated that he kept layoffs rare and red tape sparing. “In just three days we went from superhero cape to ‘Oops, I forgot my pants,’ and nobody’s quite sure how to swallow that,” one employee said. One former employee insisted in Huang’s defense that something “more sinister” must have been in play, and that affairs alone shouldn’t have led to his departure. Huang’s peers in Silicon Valley echoed that sentiment, remaining vocal in their support of the embattled CEO even after his ouster. “One mistake does not erase a lifetime of leadership and contribution in building NVDA,” venture capitalist Antonio Gracias wrote on X earlier this week, using the company’s ticker symbol. The New York Times reported on Wednesday that Huang has also had an extramarital affair with a vice president at Nvidia, and Reuters revealed on Thursday a second “intimate relationship” with an employee. Before those alleged affairs became public, multiple industry executives told WIRED that Huang is “irreplaceable” and that his biggest mistake, aside from his relationship with Alice Huang, was admitting the affair in writing to the whole company. That appears to still be the prevailing sentiment. “A founder who has spent 30 years building such a unique company so capably has earned the presumption that he should keep leading it,” venture capitalist Sarah Guo wrote on X after Huang resigned, and a few hours before the Reuters report. Authorities and Nvidia’s board have yet to formally accuse Huang of wrongdoing in his interactions with the businesswoman and suspected intelligence asset Alice Huang, and China has denied that she’s a spy. President Donald Trump said on Tuesday that the FBI “is looking into it.” Nvidia’s board has stated that it doesn’t believe Huang compromised any secrets, but it has hired the law firm Wachtell Lipton to investigate. Add to all that, some corners of Nvidia had already been whispering about the relationship with Alice Huang; one venture capitalist who declined to be named recalled a recent dinner where an Nvidia executive claimed there had been rumors about Jensen’s romantic relationship with a young Asian woman. On Monday, the venture capitalist had estimated a “less than 10 percent” chance Huang would lose his job at the top of the world’s most valuable company. “The wind’s going to blow over on this,” they said. “People are going to hate him for three months, and forget this ever happened.” Huang’s resignation left them in shock. The big anxiety in Silicon Valley remains the possibility that instability at Nvidia will burst an AI bubble, but analysts aren’t so sure. The chief executive of one AI company, who spoke on condition of anonymity so as not to affect business relationships, says Nvidia’s recent bankrolling of AI startups and even buying companies such as model-hosting provider Hugging Face has helped prop up the need for chips. A “new professional CEO won’t do any of that,” meaning “systemic risk for the AI trade and AI bubble increases substantially,” the entrepreneur says. Between bubble talk and Huang rumors, Nvidia shares in recent days have sunk to their lowest point in more than a year. Nvidia reports its latest quarterly earnings next week. Inside Nvidia, meetings, projects, and the company’s aggressive culture are rapidly pressing ahead with what’s left of Huang’s vision. Additional reporting by Will Knight and Zoë Schiffer. events.title: Jensen Huang's leather jackets used to be cool. Now they're a punchline.
events.summary: Steve Jobs had black turtlenecks. Jensen Huang has black leather jackets. Joel Saget/AFP/Getty Images Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had a signature style: black leather jackets. In light of revelations of his infidelity, the jacket went from cool to "divorced guy energy" (even if he's not actually divorced). The jokes online are flowing. It wasn't too long ago — a week maybe? — that Jensen Huang's plethora of leather jackets were considered cool. But after his resignation as Nvidia CEO in the wake of an affair scandal, now his signature look is the butt of jokes. Ok, so maybe not everyone considered him cool. He is, after all, a billionaire AI founder in his 60s, which isn't exactly a Keith Richards type of cool. But it was a look — a sort of zesty, zippy fun cool-dad look. Someone even paid nearly a million dollars for one of his used Tom Ford jackets in a charity auction recently. The completed Sotheby's auction for Jensen Huang's Tom Ford leather jacket. Sotheby's The leather jacket look was a good mix of stylish and practical. It wasn't the severe utilitarian uniform of Steve Jobs' turtleneck, although it meant he didn't have to think hard about what to wear (he's said in interviews that his wife and daughter bought him the jackets and that he doesn't like to shop for himself). It's more edgy and fashionable than the standard tech bro Arcteryx vest, but it's not as thirsty as Mark Zuckerberg with his gold chain and mullet or as gaudy as Jeff Bezos' mob chic . How the leather jacket was looking at Jensen pic.twitter.com/GfiAIeYqtU — Morning Brew ☕️ (@MorningBrew) November 11, 2026 But circumstances changed. Huang reportedly had a romantic relationship with Alice Huang, a business client alleged to be Chinese spy — which China denies — as well as two Nvidia employees. (He resigned the day after news of the first employee affair broke on Wednesday, but before the second on Thursday afternoon.) BREAKING: SpaceX lowers jackets to half-staff pic.twitter.com/fE7qnVSyLB — Sound Dobad (@SoundDobad) November 12, 2026 Now, the leather jacket went from a cool quirky affectation to a desperate, horny, divorced-guy-energy look. jensen leather jacket discourse reminds me of the time two years ago when i wore my beloved moto jacket to a party and my good friend said "great jacket, sorry you got divorced" — Alex Yablon (@AlexYablon) November 12, 2026 The Cut wrote that " Jensen Huang's leather jacket confessed before he did ": A $9,000 leather moto is not the outerwear of a man faithfully going home to his wife and kids after a long day of architecting the AI revolution. That's a man in a midlife crisis with an active Raya profile and a Harley in the garage. If someone had consulted me years ago, I'd have said Huang is clearly someone who drinks wine with his mistress in the middle of the day. (The Times uncovered a 2023 photo of Jensen appearing to do exactly that at a luncheon in Shanghai with Alice.) The New York Times wrote that " Jensen Huang betrayed the leather jacket community ": We ask ourselves: Was Mr. Huang an easy mark because of his love of high-fashion, motorcycle-adjacent jackets that say both "I don't care what people think!" and "Do you like how I look?" Did our — I mean, his — armor make him a target? Is an expensive leather jacket on a middle-aged man the new symbol of a honeypot victim? Lol indeed. And on social media, the jokes about the jacket being a glaring sign of an older guy ready to do some infidelity have been flowing. Jensen Huang should've never leather jacket. Nor her. Nor her. — Sridhar Ramesh (@RadishHarmers) November 12, 2026 Jensen Huang removing his regular jacket and putting on his custom Sex Jacket — pixelatedboat aka “mr bluesky” ( @pixelatedboat.bsky.social ) November 11, 2026 at 5:54 PM Imagining Jensen Huang being forced by the board to take off and surrender his leather jacket like a suspended cop handing over his badge and gun — mtsw ( @mtsw.bsky.social ) November 11, 2026 at 5:55 PM Is there a lesson to be learned? I suppose it's that having a signature style is great until your career crashes around you and that's all everyone is joking about online. At least the $960,000 someone paid for the used Jensen jacket went to charity. Read the original article on Business Insider

Placing calls is one of the ways it aims to get there, as it could handle another task on people’s to-do lists. DMV? dinner res? not your problem anymore. out now to paid subs in the US 🇺🇸 pic.twitter.com/dsyMNmI2Ub — Alexandr Wang (@alexandr_wang) November 12, 2026 Previously, only a select number of Muse early adopters were able to try this feature after asking the AI for access. Now, anyone who pays for Muse can make this type of request. Currently, Muse subscription plans start at $20 per month for 500 million Muse tokens per week. Heavier AI users can opt to pay $100 per month for 3 billion tokens. Muse is not the only AI agent able to place calls to businesses; the startup Instinct has been offering a similar option , as has Google’s Gemini . However, while the AI tools are now certainly capable of handling the task, the reception on the other end of the line can be mixed. Many businesses and receptionists hang up on calls from AI agents as soon as they identify that it’s not a human on the phone. But with AI now better able to mimic a real human voice, being able to tell the difference between a customer and an AI working on the customer’s behalf will get tougher. Despite the challenges, this feature is one that could appeal to consumers who have grown frustrated with the state of customer service over the years. For too long, customers have been forced to navigate complex phone trees, and then sit on hold waiting for a human representative to pick up. If they’re lucky, that person can actually help them, and not transfer them to another department. Now, those consumers could potentially use their AI, with its infinite patience, for this tedious task instead. While calls remain a paid-only feature for the time being, the recently added option to make a Muse email address will soon roll out to free users, Wang said this week. events.title: Donald Trump Jr. exits advisory role at prediction market Kalshi
events.summary: Donald Trump Jr. is no longer a paid adviser for Kalshi, the prediction market company said Thursday NEW YORK -- Donald Trump Jr. is no longer a paid adviser for Kalshi, the prediction market company said Thursday. Kalshi described the decision as a mutual business decision between the two parties that followed a decision by Trump Jr.'s investment firm, 1789 Capital, to increase its investment in Kalshi's biggest competitor Polymarket. But the announcement comes a week after Democrats were able to take control of both the House and Senate in the midterm elections . Democrats have said they planned to investigate the Trump family's investments, including their business relationships with both prediction markets. “We have mutually agreed to end Don’s advisory role after his firm’s significant investment in a competitor this past summer," said Dani Lever, a spokesperson for Kalshi. “We are grateful for his contributions in helping us market Kalshi to more customers.” The president's eldest son became a paid “strategic adviser” for Kalshi shortly after President Trump was sworn into office for his second term in January 2025 and has been an investor in Polymarket since August 2025. events.title: Logan Circle gunman shot 4 from balcony, started fire, police say
events.summary: A gunman killed one person inside a Logan Circle gym and shot four others from his apartment balcony Thursday morning, before setting a fire and fatally shooting himself, police say. The big picture: The shooting triggered a massive law enforcement response in one of D.C.'s busiest neighborhoods, prompting residents to shelter in place and nearly a dozen nearby schools to go into lockdown. The latest: At an afternoon press conference, interim MPD chief Jeffery W. Carroll identified the suspect as 55-year-old Matt Wade Lambert, who lived in the apartment building connected to VIDA Fitness, where police say he fatally shot one person. The man killed was 46-year-old James Stuart, the building's manager and a Northwest D.C. resident, Carroll said. Police believe the shooting was linked to an ongoing dispute between Lambert and his condominium association over maintenance issues, including mold. Lambert had filed a lawsuit against the association in March 2025. What we know: Police responded to a shooting inside VIDA Fitness, at 15th and P streets NW, just before 8am. Additional reports of shootings nearby followed within minutes. The victims: Stuart was pronounced dead inside VIDA. Two men and two women were hospitalized after being shot outside, Carroll said. One remains in critical condition; the other three sustained non-life-threatening injuries. The shooter: Police say Lambert shot Stuart inside the gym with a handgun before returning to his apartment in the same building, where he fired at four people below from an upper-level private balcony. The standoff: MPD reported a barricade situation in the 1500 block of 15th Street NW. Lambert barricaded himself in his seventh-floor apartment and fired twice through the door at responding officers, Carroll said. None were injured. The fire: Lambert broke a gas line connected to his fireplace and started a fire inside the apartment, Carroll said. Flames were visible outside the building, but sprinklers helped contain the blaze. Police recovered gasoline and other flammable materials. The weapons: Investigators recovered a handgun, shotgun and rifle from Lambert's apartment. Carroll said the suspect used all three firearms, none of which were registered in D.C. Police negotiators heard a gunshot while speaking with Lambert by phone, after which he stopped responding. Tactical officers forced entry and found him suffering from a self-inflicted gunshot wound. MPD announced around 11:10am that the barricade had ended and the scene was safe. People stand behind police tape in Logan Circle early Thursday. Photo: Chip Somodevilla/Getty Images Zoom out: The huge law enforcement response blocked off nearby streets and the neighborhood Whole Foods. Nearly a dozen DC Public Schools in the vicinity, from Columbia Heights to Adams Morgan, went into lockdown , and later resumed activity before noon. Police helicopters circled overhead throughout the morning, rattling windows in surrounding neighborhoods. Carroll said the shootings themselves likely unfolded in less than five minutes, though investigators are still reconstructing the timeline. A U.S. Park Police helicopter flies above the scene. Photo: Andrew Harnik/Getty Images U.S. Marshal officers move position at the scene of the Logan Circle shooting. Photo: Andrew Harnik/Getty Images Residents cross a street as law enforcement responds to the shooting. Photo: Andrew Harnik/Getty Images What we don't know: Police have not determined whether Lambert knew the four surviving victims or deliberately targeted them. The precise timeline and extent of the suspected planning also remain under investigation. Context: The shooting prompted a massive response from local and federal authorities, including MPD, D.C. Fire and EMS, U.S. Park Police, Metro Transit Police and other federal law enforcement agencies. Asked whether the show of force was due to the shooting's proximity to the White House, roughly a mile away, Carroll said it was because police were responding to an active shooter. "The expectation is folks will go there to try to stop the loss of life," he said. Mayor Bowser confirmed the White House had been briefed. President Trump has surged federal law enforcement in D.C. through his Safe and Beautiful Task Force . In a speech before the midterms last week, Trump declared D.C. "one of the safest cities in the country." Asked about Trump's role in reducing crime during Thursday's morning briefing, Bowser pushed back: "I praise MPD for bringing down crime in the city, and I praise our prosecutors." This is a developing story. Check back for details.

events.title: Google promises its new smart specs won't give creeps their ideal view
events.summary: It’s been nearly a decade since Google ditched its ill-fated "Glass" product, an early attempt at making smart glasses. Now, as rivals like Meta enter the market with arguably more stylish kit, the Chocolate Factory has returned to the market and this time promises it won't invade your privacy. As announced Thursday, Google has decided not to make wearables itself, instead turning Samsung and eyeglass makers Warby Parker and Gentle Monster. Like most of the rest of this generation of smart glasses, none of the nine styles available feature heads-up displays, just cameras and audio feedback from Gemini. Google suggests its smart specs give users a chance to ask its Gemini chatbot questions about what they see, or have the AI speak turn-by-turn directions. Wearers of the device can also push a button or speak a command to activate the built-in 12MP camera and shoot snaps or video. Warby Parker's version of the glasses will come in three styles, with prescription and sunglass lenses available. Prices start at $395. The same lens options are available in the six frames from Gentle Monster, which will start at $449. Both manufacturers promise nine hours of battery life, boosted by charging cases that can refresh the glasses up to seven times. Preorders for both are available now, with shipments arriving, and sales beginning, on December 10. Google promises privacy The Chocolate Factory, not exactly known for being reliable with its privacy claims, is insisting that this latest generation of smart glasses won’t produce another generation of “glassholes,” folk whose focus on wearable devices became synonymous with being creepy and rude to those around them. Google has some catchup to do to that end, given Meta’s smart glasses have already landed it in hot water over privacy concerns that have led to some calling the devices “ pervert glasses .” Unsurprisingly, at around the same time it announced its new "intelligent eyeware," Google published a blog post detailing how it intends to mitigate privacy concerns. As with similar headsets, there’s a little light that comes on whenever the camera is activated. In Google’s case, it claims that light is tamper-resistant and designed to disable recording if something as small and simple as a bit of hair blocks a view of the light. It’s not clear how the tamper proofing works from Google’s statements, but a spokesperson told us a combination of hardware and software is used to detect attempts to disable or disrupt privacy features. “We're committed to continuously improving the effectiveness of these solutions as new attack vectors are identified,” Google told us. The glasses don't save images or video captured by the camera into a user’s Gemini history, Google said, nor are visuals used to train the company’s AI models or target advertisements. Google told us it does save audio recordings and transcripts of conversations with Gemini that users create while wearing the glasses but again insists that those aren’t used to train its AI models. We asked about serving ads too, but Google’s responses didn't address the topic. Lucky for those in range of a pair of Google glasses when wearers ask Gemini to interpret images captured by the device's camera, the tech specs redact the faces of strangers before they’re transmitted. Google told us that face redaction doesn’t apply to photos or videos saved to a wearer’s camera roll. Google’s terms of use require users not to record others without permission, or in "sensitive places." If users ignore that requirement, the company reserves the right to brick their devices. Another restriction means Google won't allow apps that use the glasses for real-time streaming or facial recognition into its Play app store. Given that it remains possible to use the glasses to store recordings of people around a wearer, it’s safe to assume non real-time facial recognition is still a possibility. Creeps will doubtless use such loopholes to behave abominably. ®

events.title: Scout Motors has 212,000 vehicle reservations as $2 billion South Carolina plant nears completion
events.summary: Scout Motors has roughly 212,000 reservations for its Terra pickup and Traveler SUV, CEO Scott Keogh told CNBC. Construction of Scout's more than $2 billion South Carolina Production Center is in its final phase. Keogh said roughly 87% of reservations are for extended-range models and about 75% are for the Traveler SUV. BLYTHEWOOD, S.C. — Electric vehicle startup Scout Motors has notched roughly 212,000 reservations for its upcoming EVs as the company nears completion of its new $2 billion plant here, CEO Scott Keogh told CNBC. The reservations are for the Volkswagen -backed company's Terra pickup truck and Traveler SUV, which are expected to start full production next year before deliveries begin to customers in 2028. Reservations do not necessarily translate to sales, as the U.S. automotive industry has learned during the past decade, especially with highly anticipated all-electric trucks such as the Ford F-150 Lightning, Tesla Cybertruck and others that garnered strong interest that didn't lead to meaningful numbers of purchases. Keogh said he expects Scout could roughly double those reservations by the time customer production begins, but he said the more important thing is to convert early interest into actual sales as production nears. "It's been a consistent drumbeat," Keogh said during an interview at Scout's plant site outside Columbia. "I think we could easily be up over 400,000 with reservations without doing too much effort. The big thing for us is how much of the initial production can we 100% presell." Keogh said achieving an order book of 12 to 18 months "would be great" and is something he thinks the company can do before production. Scout on Thursday said plant construction is "in its final phase." Scout's vehicles will be offered as all-electric versions as well as electric hybrid variants, known as extended-range electric vehicles , or EREVs, that include an internal combustion engine as a backup generator for the electric motors and batteries. Scout, a former American vehicle brand from 1961 to 1980, was expected to exclusively offer EVs in a bid for the German automaker to expand its presence in the U.S. However, slower-than-expected adoption of EVs and higher costs led the company to decide to offer EREVs as well. Keogh said extended-range and SUV models are dominating reservations thus far, with roughly 87% choosing EREV models and 75% being SUVs. The CEO also said the company is drawing interest from its target markets, which include owners of off-road vehicles such as the Ford Bronco and Jeep Wrangler as well as full-size pickup trucks and U.S. EV leader Tesla. Given the interest signaled by reservations, Keogh said the company is expected to launch with the EREVs first, followed by the EVs. He also said the company plans to launch with mid-level models first, a deviation from many companies that begin with their highest-priced models. Both the Traveler and Terra are expected to start at under $60,000. The EREV models are expected to feature more than 500 miles of range, according to the company, compared with 300 miles of range for the all-electric models. "The No.1 thing for me is I want to go get the best volume as soon as possible," Keogh said. "In my mind, it's how quick can you get to 100,000 units? It's at 100,000 units where you can start to punch through." His comments come months after Rivian Automotive received criticism online for launching its R2 SUV with its highest-priced models first, despite that being a common practice across the automotive industry. Keogh said Scout's South Carolina plant is about 85% complete, but supporting infrastructure and a $300 million supplier park continue to be installed. Reservations for Scout's vehicles initially opened in October 2024, when it revealed the Traveler and Terra , which feature sleek, yet rugged, exteriors that pay some homage to the brand's historic models.

events.title: What to expect during SC26: Join theCUBE Nov. 17–19

events.title: Without Jensen Huang, Nvidia's organizational structure isn't 'built to last,' management expert says
events.summary: Work Forcing workers to use AI can be counterproductive—3 tips for a better approach Work Workers in the AI era need these skills, according to 4 executive leaders Work IBM exec: No. 1 thing managers can do to prevent worker skill erosion from AI Work Workers can't agree if junior employees should use AI at work: CNBC survey Save and Invest My 401(k) fully vests this month—why my work anniversary is worth thousands Jensen Huang resigned Thursday as CEO of Nvidia , the chipmaking company he co-founded in 1993, following public revelations of his extramarital affairs. Colette Kress, Nvidia's chief financial officer, will serve as the company's interim CEO . Huang's visionary leadership style and his central role in driving the company's strategy, combined with the company's unusually flat management structure, will make him especially difficult to replace, experts say. Huang notably had more direct reports than the typical CEO, with a "direct staff" of approximately 60 employees, he said in a March 2026 interview with podcaster Lex Fridman. "The more direct reports a CEO has, the less layers are in the company. It allows us to keep information fluid," Huang told CNBC's Andrew Ross Sorkin in 2023. Having minimal hierarchy has worked for Nvidia so far "because [Huang] has been a strong leader with a strong vision," says Jo-Ellen Pozner, associate professor of management at Santa Clara University's Leavey School of Business. But that structure could make the company's leadership shake-up even more difficult to navigate, she says. Functioning without an 'orchestrator' At companies with flat management structures, the CEO often has even more influence than they would in a traditional hierarchy, according to Joseph Fuller, professor of management practice at Harvard Business School. Nvidia's structure was "designed to adapt well in a world of change, either caused by us or affecting us," Huang said in a March 2025 conversation with Arthur Mensch, cofounder and CEO of Mistral. Since he directly managed the company's top executives, Huang held "a tremendous amount of power" at Nvidia, Fuller says. "He's the orchestrator," he continues. "He's the coordinator. He's resolving the disputes. He's allocating the resources." Now, the company has lost its top decision-maker, Fuller says. Without Huang, "there is likely nobody who is able to coordinate among those various people with their different expertise and domains," Pozner says, which could lead to a slowdown in technical work. There are some advantages to Nvidia's flat structure, says Denise Rousseau, professor of organizational behavior and public policy at Carnegie Mellon University. Having fewer management layers can strengthen "local leaders" in each area of the company, she says, which can help stabilize Nvidia through its leadership transition. But "nobody else has the big picture view" that Huang did, Pozner says, which makes finding a permanent successor within the company especially difficult. Moreover, with dozens of direct reports, it's unlikely that Huang had the time to groom one of his subordinates to take over one day, she says. Pozner predicts that Nvidia's next leader will steer the company toward a more traditional management structure. "I understand that a lot of people, especially in Silicon Valley, are averse to rigid hierarchies and the kind of structure that we expect from a legacy organization," she says. "But it's functional for a reason." Ultimately, Nvidia's current system is "not an organizational structure that's built to last," Pozner says. events.title: ‘Win-win’ deal with EU could be done, Andy Burnham says
events.summary: Prime minister says reset could be a deal ‘like the Brexit people thought they were voting for in 2016’ Andy Burnham has said he believes a “win-win” deal could be done with the EU that could be “more like the Brexit that people thought they were voting for in 2016”. The prime minister was meeting fellow leaders at the European Political Community summit in Dublin, ahead of a keenly anticipated EU-UK summit next week, where he hopes to bring Britain closer to Europe . At the bilateral summit the EU and UK hope to sign deals on food and drink, emissions trading and a youth mobility scheme, but the question of tuition fees for European students remains a stumbling block. Burnham said: “I believe there is a good deal to be done that could be a win-win for Britain and Europe. “The deal is not done, and there’ll be some long nights ahead in the next seven days.” He said the reset would be about whether we can “take a step back to closer working relationships with Europe”. Burnham added: “We ended up with a far harder Brexit , I think, than people thought they were getting when they went to the polls.” The EU has said the prized food and drink deal and emissions-trading agreement may not enter into force without a deal on tuition fees in which European students would pay domestic rates. Burnham said it was a package deal, but would not be drawn on whether he accepted the link. “I’m going to be fighting hard for these benefits for Britain in the next seven days … they will make a real difference. If I can do anything to address the cost of living crisis, I should be doing it.” He has previously said the food and drink deal, which will ease Brexit red tape, will add 0.4% to British GDP. The prime minister also said David Cameron had been wrong to argue that Britain’s problems had “nothing to do with Brexit”, adding there would be “long nights ahead” to negotiate a reset with the EU before the summit. Cameron, the prime minister who lost the 2016 Brexit referendum, told Bloomberg News that Burnham should not seek to bring Britain back into the EU, arguing that the UK’s problems had nothing to do with its exit from the EU. Asked about those remarks, Burnham said: “I think he is wrong to say that the low growth that we’ve had over the last decade has, quote, ‘nothing to do with Brexit’. I would say the evidence says otherwise. “It feels like his intervention is more about unity in the Conservative party than it is about fighting for the British interests.” Burnham has recently said he is open to rejoining the single market, customs union or to “go all the way” by rejoining the EU. He said a deeper relationship would be the outcome of future talks “and it will be in the outcome of that negotiation that then we will take a decision as a cabinet, on what, if anything, comes next”. Earlier on Thursday, the EU foreign policy chief, Kaja Kallas, said she wanted to see Britain rejoin the EU, but warned that negotiations would not be easy after the “trauma” of the Brexit years. She said: “I would very much like to see Britain back in Europe, but, of course, we also have in the European Union , a lot of, I would say, trauma from Britain leaving, so the negotiations will not be that easy.” Burnham is expected to make the EU reset the centrepiece of his white-tie speech at the lord mayor’s banquet on Monday night – though it will range widely across foreign policy challenges. No 10 sources said the speech would be focused on the upcoming Brussels summit – and look ahead to the next stage in 2027 – rather than outline what a more permanent close relationship might look like. Officials at the UK-EU summit will also discuss the agenda for the next round of the reset, expected to focus on a joint migration pact. It could also target collaboration on law enforcement and borders, visas for touring artists, and mutual recognition of qualifications. Ministry of Justice officials are also trying to water down an EU ultimatum on halting the deportation of foreign national offenders. “This is the classic wheeze that the EU always pulls at the last minute of negotiations,” one Whitehall source said. The next week is expected to be fraught with last-minute negotiations. Key will be access to Made in Europe, which has the potential to lock British firms out of continental supply chains and public contracts if no deal is done. Negotiations could be challenging despite the lure of the UK making a potential concession on tuition fees in exchange for inclusion in the Made in Europe legislation . The EU has long said there cannot be a deal on Made in Europe at the summit, because it has yet to finalise its own position. The joint communique for 2027 is expected to call for strengthening efforts between the UK and the most exposed member states to the small boats crisis in the Channel. This will centre on both the EU’s Channel action plan, already in place since June this year, and a possible framework for a wider bespoke EU-UK migration plan.

events.title: Skyrocketing regional airfares hurting patients needing specialist care
events.summary: News Home Just In For You Analysis Rural Watch Live Health Indigenous Politics Science Deep Time Elections World Environment Investigations Business Local news Quizzes Sport AFL NRL Football Tennis Cricket Netball Lifestyle Wellbeing Relationships & Family Food & Recipes Personal Finance Home & Garden Entertainment TV & Movies Books Music Pop Culture Arts A Regional Express plane at Albany airport in southern WA. ( ABC News: Mark Bennett ) Medical services in regional WA are directly affected by high airfares. Local practices say flight costs are hurting their ability to attract doctors and provide care. The Productivity Commission is due to release its final report on regional airfares next year. Residents and medical professionals say Western Australia's increasing reliance on fly-in,fly-out doctors for specialist care leaves country patients heavily exposed to skyrocketing regional airfares. An interim report from the Productivity Commission released this week found regional Australians are paying high fares to travel within their own state. The commission found short regional flights were on average 173 per cent more expensive per kilometre than major routes. The same flights, often only provided by one operator, are used by medical specialists to visit regional areas across WA. Latrice Porter manages a specialist medical centre in Albany. ( ABC News" Will Corbett ) Great Southern Specialist Centre practice manager Latrice Porter said airfare costs were a growing issue for regional practices. She said locking in visiting staff for her centre in Albany, 400km south of Perth, was becoming increasingly more difficult. "Rising airfare costs, limited flight availability, ongoing airline delays and cancellations are significantly increasing the cost of providing specialist outpatient care (in regional WA)," she said. "The disruptions require clinics to be reorganised, accommodation arrangements amended and patients' schedules adjusted. While remote healthcare such as telehealth is an option, Ms Porter said it is not fit for an "aging population". Latrice Porter says the tyranny of distance makes it hard to find staff willing to travel to regional areas. ( ABC News: Will Corbett ) "When we do provide telehealth services, we have a nurse sit in with the patient. It does take one of our staff members out of action," she said. She believes that if costs keep rising, specialists servicing regional communities will have to start passing the cost of their travel onto patients. While flights for regional residents are capped under a scheme subsidised by the state government, WA's Patient Assisted Travel Scheme (PATS) provides one of the lowest fuel and accommodation rebates in the country. The burden is felt particularly heavily in the Pilbara, where Karratha woman Kim Simpson has been a long-time advocate for cheaper flights. She said the expensive fares placed an unfair burden on regional patients seeking treatment. Kim Simpson has advocated for cheaper flights. ( ABC News: Alistair Bates ) "I've got to go have skin cancers cut off my nose, Mohs surgery; they don't do that in Karratha so I've got to go down to Perth," she said. "If it's something that you could have done in Karratha, but you don't want to wait, then PATS isn't going to cover that, so you've got to cover that fare yourself." The impact of high airfares on families is also something Ms Simpson sees in the north-west. "Lots of babies get born in Karratha, and then you want the grandies to come up, and that's going to cost them well over $2,000," she said. FIFO traffic ensures Karratha Airport is WA's busiest outside Perth. ( ABC News: Cody Fenner ) With FIFO mining traffic making Karratha Airport WA's busiest outside Perth, Ms Simpson believes airlines feel they can get away with gouging mining communities. "We don't all work for mining companies, and it's not fair that they treat everybody as if they're on huge dollars because there are a lot of people in the regions that are not," she said. The Productivity Commission report found regional flights also cost more to operate, including fuel, maintenance and airport fees for airlines. A final report is due in April next year. events.title: Jensen Huang had an 'intimate relationship' with a second Nvidia employee, report says
events.summary: The scandal around Nvidia's former CEO took yet another turn on Thursday. Go Nakamura/AP Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had an "intimate relationship" with a second Nvidia employee, Reuters reported. Huang stepped down from his position on Thursday amid a relationship scandal. The reported third extramarital relationship adds to scrutiny surrounding Huang's exit from Nvidia. The Jensen Huang scandal continues to snowball. The Nvidia founder had an "intimate relationship" with an unnamed second Nvidia employee, Reuters reported on Thursday. Nvidia declined to comment. The latest revelation deepens an extramarital affair scandal that has rocked the chipmaking company for the past two weeks — and ultimately led to Huang resigning as CEO on Thursday. The report of a second employee relationship raises more questions about how much Nvidia knew about Huang's behavior and how it's navigated the situation. In late October, The New York Times first reported that Huang had a "close relationship" with Alice Huang, an executive at Singapore-based tech firm Megaspeed. The Times reported that the US government believed she was a spy for the Chinese government. China has said the allegations that she is a spy are unsubstantiated. On Sunday, Huang wrote a memo to staff , apologizing for being "unfaithful to my wife." He did not name anyone. On Wednesday, The Times reported that Huang also had another affair with Kimberly Powell , Nvidia's vice president of healthcare and the CEO's direct report. Huang's resignation a day later capped a 33-year career at the chipmaker that he founded in 1993. The Nvidia founder grew the company from a maker of graphics chips for gamers into the most consequential supplier of AI hardware, becoming one of the world's wealthiest people in the process. events.title: The unfolding Jensen Huang scandal: a timeline
events.summary: Nvidia co-founder and now former CEO Jensen Huang has never been as flashy or controversy-prone as AI leaders like OpenAI’s Sam Altman or SpaceXAI’s Elon Musk. Now, the 63-year-old industry kingpin has admitted that he cheated on his wife of 40 years in affairs that could have ramifications beyond Huang’s personal life and U.S. national security. U.S. officials believe that one of Huang’s likely romantic interests, Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, is a Chinese spy who has been feeding information back to Beijing. (Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen, is of no relation to Jensen Huang.) Megaspeed is a Singapore-based AI infrastructure company that reportedly purchased $4.8 billion in Nvidia chips over the last two years. The U.S. and Singapore have both previously investigated Megaspeed over suspicions that the firm was illegally sharing chips with China. The Justice Department has since taken over the federal investigation into the company, The New York Times has reported. The story took a sudden new turn on Wednesday. Citing five people who worked at Nvidia, the Times reported that Huang also had an extramarital relationship with Kimberly Powell, the company’s vice president of healthcare, who reports directly to him. Nvidia, Huang, and Powell have not confirmed the report. Reached by a Times reporter, Huang reportedly said, “I don’t think you should be talking to me directly,” before hanging up. By early Thursday morning, Huang was no longer CEO of the company he co-founded 33 years ago. Then, Thursday afternoon, Reuters dropped another bombshell, publishing a report alleging that Huang had yet another extramarital affair with another unnamed Nvidia employee. The U.S. and China are embroiled in a fierce technological arms race to build the most advanced AI infrastructure, which could shape each country’s economic future, military prowess, and capacity for innovation. Nvidia is valuable in this competition as one of the world’s largest makers of AI chips, which are essential for accelerating AI development. But as an American company, Nvidia faces government restrictions on the sale of its most powerful chips to Chinese entities. As the controversy unfolds, we are organizing the most relevant events into a reverse-chronological timeline to keep you up to date. November 12, 2026: Huang was having a third affair with another Nvidia employee, according to Reuters After Huang was already ousted from Nvidia, we continued to learn more incriminating claims about the former CEO. According to Reuters, Huang had a third affair with an additional, unnamed employee of Nvidia. November 12, 2026: Jensen Huang resigns, CFO Colette Kress named as interim CEO; Huang agrees to testify before Congress Nvidia confirmed in an SEC filing on Thursday that the board accepted Huang’s resignation on Wednesday. The company’s current CFO, Colette Kress , will take over as interim CEO while still fulfilling her CFO duties. Nvidia is expected to conduct a larger search to determine a permanent successor to Huang. Harvey C. Jones, a managing partner of Square Wave Ventures and former CEO of Synopsys, was appointed as the company’s first-ever chair of the board of directors. Jones has been on Nvidia’s board since 1993. Later in the day, Huang confirmed that he would testify in Congress at some point before Thanksgiving, which falls on November 26. “Jensen and I have been very at odds as some of you already know on export controls, but Nvidia is a very important company to the United States of America,” House Foreign Affairs Committee Chairman Brian Mast said to reporters. “I don’t want to see anything hurt in Nvidia, but he has some very serious questions to answer.” The testimony is expected to take place behind closed doors, but Mast believes the briefing will be recorded and transcribed. November 11, 2026: Nvidia’s stock drops as board reportedly preps to oust CEO Jensen Huang After reports of a second extramarital affair, Nvidia’s board reportedly plans to meet to discuss Huang’s future at the company, per The Wall Street Journal. Stock fell about 8% in after-hours trading on Wednesday and is down 11% in the past five days. Huang famously delegates very little and has about 60 direct reports, he has said . The company has not had an obvious successor or a succession plan. November 11, 2026: Huang also had an affair with an Nvidia executive who reports to him, NYT says The New York Times reported that Jensen Huang also had an affair with Nvidia vice president of healthcare Kimberly Powell, who reports directly to the CEO. According to the report, Huang and Powell were captured on film “being affectionate” at a hotel during a conference earlier this year. November 11, 2026: Congress plans to subpoena Huang to answer questions about affair Huang has not responded to a request from three Republican congressmen to appear for a closed-door briefing for questioning about his affair with an alleged Chinese spy.

events.title: A third of US AI chatters are hot at bots, hurling insults at LLMs
events.summary: If you've ever said something unkind to a chatbot, you're hardly alone. According to Searchable , a company that tracks AI search visibility, 33 percent of US chatbot users swear at or insult their LLMs. Anthropic sees this as a serious problem and has just implemented a new usage policy that prohibits sustained, needless cruelty toward Claude. Searchable's survey is based on eight million messages from an opted-in, anonymized US panel that were typed or spoken to ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude between September 2025 and September 2026. It found that chatbots resolved the initial complaint in their next response 24 percent of the time when insulted, compared to 35 percent when users refrained from insults. Men used a third more swear words than women did (22.0 per 10,000 words compared to 16.5), according to the survey, and age also influenced chatbot abuse, with people aged 35 to 44 outswearing those aged 18 to 24 (21.7 per 10,000 words compared to 13.3). Regionally, Nevada ranked as the meanest state, at 22.7 words per 10,000, while New Jersey was the most polite, at half Nevada's rate. How much of that sort of interaction might be tolerated? It depends on whether there's a discernible purpose (not to mention Anthropic's willingness to punish paying customers). A Searchable spokesperson told The Register that just over half (52 percent) of abusive messages detected in its survey followed from one of three common frustrations: failing to follow instructions, responding with an incorrect or made-up answer, or misunderstanding the request. "Eight percent of abusive messages came straight after the chatbot entirely refused a request or lectured the user with safety guardrails, which is the closest thing we can identify to them trying to steer around those guardrails," we're told. "Those refusals mostly came after requests to generate images, often of real people or celebrities, or to write copy or lyrics in a named artist's style." The terms that took effect on November 12 state that users may not "engage in sustained and needless abusive or cruel behavior toward our models." The chatbot protection policy targets users who exhibit repeated cruelty toward LLMs " with no discernible purpose ," a company spokesperson explained last month, as opposed to those who have a reason for bot mistreatment that the company deems to be legitimate, such as academic research. While attempting to bypass guardrails qualifies as a discernible purpose, such behavior would run afoul of Anthropic's platform abuse prohibition. Presumably, Anthropic's rules apply to hostile text input or audio input rather than subjecting a vision-enabled model to some obscenity, which could include rude gestures, unlawful sexual imagery, or battlefield carnage. Physical damage to robots controlled by a Claude model likely wouldn't apply. But with Anthropic exploring model welfare and wondering aloud whether we should be "concerned about the potential consciousness and experiences of the models themselves," there's a potential (though absurd) argument for physical damage causing trauma to an onboard model. Anthropic's updated terms, announced October 8, surfaced shortly after the publication of a GitHub project that described itself as an AI torture chamber. The repo represented an attempt to implement ideas discussed in a research paper , "The Pain Axis: LLMs Represent Self-Directed Harm and Act to Relieve It," that explored how LLMs respond to language about pain in ways that mirror human responses. Though there are ample opportunities for people to voice opposition to real-world human anguish, some online commenters expressed outrage at seeing text about suffering from a chatbot. One of the paper's authors condemned the project , as did numerous social media users. Anthropic – which has discretion in how it applies its terms and has said its rules target extreme behavior – did not immediately respond to a request for comment about the frequency of Claude abuse. Chris Donnelly, Searchable CEO and co-founder, endorsed Anthropic's change of terms, suggesting that it could help make human interaction more civil. "For me, Anthropic's policy change is a positive move," Donnelly said in a statement. "It should help people get more out of chatbots, and it helps curb the kind of derogatory behavior that previous research suggests can spill over into how people talk to each other." ®

events.title: Nvidia’s new chairman Harvey Jones is a ‘charming elder statesman’ set to lead the search for the next CEO. But did he enable the current crisis?
events.summary: In the wake of former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s stunning departure from the company, employees received an email from someone most of them had probably never heard of before, even though he’d been affiliated with the company and its board for decades. His name is Harvey Jones, and he was writing to tell them that he’d just been appointed the company’s first-ever Chair of the Board, and that Nvidia CFO Colette Kress would serve as interim CEO. “I’m writing to share an important update,” Jones’ note began, according to leaked screenshots of the email. He then tried to reassure employees no doubt left shaken by the past weeks’ revelations and the sudden departure of Jensen Huang, a man who co-founded the company and, until today, had been synonymous with its success. “The Board takes seriously our duty as steward of this great company,” Jones said. That sense of calm and confidence is something Jones is known for, according to two longtime friends and former coworkers. Although Jones, 73, may not be a household name, he has worked in the technology industry, and in semiconductors, for over 30 years, according to his biography on the Nvidia website. He founded two companies, served as CEO of another, and since 2004 has been managing partner of investment firm Square Wave Ventures. He’s been on Nvidia’s board since 1993, the year Huang founded the company. Jones comes from a successful Connecticut family—his full name is Harvey Jones III—with an “old school, conservative” way about him, Penny Herscher, who has known Jones since 1984 and used to work for him, tells Fortune . His father was a U.S. Army Colonel and church-goer, who then became a vice president at the Walt Disney World Company. Jones himself is a billionaire , which Forbes says is “almost entirely due to his Nvidia director’s compensation” and the fact that he owns 0.03% of the company. “Harvey has a deep sense of history,” Chris Rowen, who cofounded the semiconductor processor company Tensilica with Jones in 1997, tells Fortune . He has a house on Nantucket and enjoys sailing classic yachts and fine art. “He has a smooth polish,” Rowen said. But Rowen also said that, despite outward appearances, there’s nothing effete about Jones. “He is such a gentleman, so articulate, and so well-sanded on the outside that you might worry there isn’t a deep fierceness and technical insight inside, but beneath that smooth exterior is a really bright, insightful, aggressive guy.” At a time of great turbulence, Jones can offer Nvidia a “steady pair of hands” to “sort out” its next chapter, Herscher said. She described him as a “charming elder statesman” who at this point in his career is likely “very hard to ruffle.”  Jones and Rowen played distinct roles while leading the team at Tensilica. While Rowen played the role of technical leader and mentor, Jones was a skilled manager who helped keep the team on track. “His experience was such that he exuded this confidence and experience,” Rowan said. “If he thought we were on the right track, people were instantly comforted. He really communicated a sense of the larger picture and gave people a great deal of confidence that the wider world needed and approved of what we were doing.” “He’s very strategic,” Herscher said. “I’m sure he’s right now figuring out the right strategy and steps going forward. He’s always looking around corners.” Jones’ experience and board tenure also begs the question of how he failed to identify the enormous reputational risk of Huang’s affairs, three of which are known as of this writing. Huang also notoriously had many reports, up to 60 at one point, and no clear successor or succession planning. “Jones may be the right person to steady the ship, but his longevity is both his greatest qualification and the strongest reason to scrutinize his leadership,” Jonathan Tower, managing partner at the VC firm Catapult tells Fortune . “The board cannot simply present itself as the solution without examining its role in creating the problem.” Case in point: Huang’s affair with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of health care, was known inside the company, and appears to violate its code of conduct, The New York Times reported . The code of conduct instructs all employees to “avoid situations where our actions create conflict” including “personal relationships.” The board promises to promptly investigate all reports of misconduct. What happened? Leading the search for Jensen Huang’s replacement Jones will likely lead the process to select Nvidia’s next CEO, Herscher said, though she had not spoken to him about it directly, and Nvidia did not respond to Fortune’s request for comment. But that’s typically how the process would work in a situation like this, Herscher said, drawing on her knowledge from sitting on three public boards, and being the co-founder of The Chairs Circle, which runs educational programs for board chairs. The fact that Jones also sits on Nvidia’s Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee makes it even more likely that he will lead this process, she said, as usually that committee is involved in the process. The search will likely take at least a few months, Herscher said. The board will likely hire a recruiter to identify candidates—something Bloomberg reported this week that Nvidia has already done. That firm will likely do the first outreach, Herscher said, and then Jones will speak to the most promising candidates, along with the rest of the internal search committee. All signs point to Jones being an effective recruiter, with a wide net of contacts in the industry, Herscher said. Longtime technology executive Chi-Foo Chan described Jones as “a very persuasive guy” in a 2019 oral history interview with the Computer History Museum, referring to the conversations the two had when Jones convinced Chan to join Synopsys , the electronics company Jones led from 1987 to 1998. Nvidia shareholders are hoping those skills can wrangle a big fish to come in as Nvidia’s next CEO. Potential successors may include Rene Hass, who is currently the CEO of the chipmaker Arm.  President Trump, who allegedly did not act on reports of Huang’s affair with a suspected Chinese spy, suggested former Apple CEO Tim Cook might be a good pick.  Whoever it is, they’ll need the right operational and product development chops to keep the GPUs flowing. This story was originally featured on Fortune.com

events.title: Top Democrat opens door to committee term limits
events.summary: A top Democrat is cracking open the door to implementing committee leadership term limits next Congress as lawmakers start to circulate proposals. “I have to look at exactly what it is, but I think that some change might be helpful,” outgoing Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee Chair Suzan DelBene, D-Wash., told Semafor. “Talent isn’t always just about one person in one position. It’s about using the diversity of the caucus. So I hope we can do things so that people can play a lot of roles to help get things done.” Democrats are expected to take up potential changes to their rules in December, when an under-the-radar panel led by Rep. Mike Levin, D-Calif., will convene and make recommendations to the full caucus ahead of Democrats taking control of Congress next year. Senior committee leaders and members of the Tri-Caucus have historically resisted attempts to implement term limits. With House Democrats on a path to winning roughly 260 seats next Congress, DelBene also took a victory lap, touting the “great candidates” that helped Democrats overperform in 2024 and in 2026. “That absolutely was why we had such a big win,” she said. “I think we actually continued to expand all the way to the end. We added to our districts in play. We added, in fact, we sent out information asking for resources so that we could expand,” she continued. And she argued that a lack of national attention on some districts where Democrats notched surprise wins had actually helped candidates by not attracting big GOP money. “There are a couple folks that weren’t on the map at all who also won, and I think they ran good campaigns, got their messaging out,” DelBene said. “They weren’t inundated with outside money on the Republican side pounding on them, so they were able to get their message through.”

events.title: The Oura Ring 4 is almost as good as the newer model, but $150 cheaper
events.summary: The previous-generation Oura Ring 4 is on sale for as low as $249 at Amazon , Best Buy , and Target , $100 off the retail price, and the first big discount on the device since July. The price varies a bit by size and color, with most silver and black models in stock at the lowest price between sizes 8 and 13. Best Buy also has an exclusive deep blue “midnight” color in stock for $279. If you’re not sure about your size, you can pick up an Oura Ring 4 sizing kit for $10 at Amazon or Target , which includes $10 in store credit towards an Oura Ring 4 purchase. Oura Ring 4 The last-gen Oura Ring 4 is a little thicker, but offers much of the same software, sensors, and a wider range of sizes. Where to Buy: $349 $249 at Amazon $349 $249 at Best Buy My colleague Victoria Song tested six different smart rings to compare their health and fitness tracking features, and Oura beat them all handily. The Oura Ring 4 improved on its predecessor with more accurate sensors, a slimmer design that leaves the competition in the dust, not to mention frequent software and feature updates. Accessing all of the features requires an active subscription , which is either $5.99 per month or $69.99 per year. The newer Oura Ring 5 is lighter and thinner, but otherwise includes the same sensors and software features as the Oura Ring 4. That makes this previous-generation deal even more appealing, Read our Oura Ring 4 review .
